judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: The missing full stop and the number slip ('the last [Group] who went after... is still missing') look like real shipped text, and the plain fatalism ('He'll never get it back') sounds like Nox. The third line runs a little long.

items.label: B
items.critique: The first two barks have an odd, lively Nox feel, but the third is a self-introduction that sets up lore ('to keep the high road safe for traders'), which Westwood's idle townsfolk rarely do.

items.label: C
items.critique: Gossip that takes sides, a dry joke about a woman in charge, and a short closing exclamation ('Only fools and warriors...'). Plain speech with real character, very much the campaign's voice.

items.label: D
items.critique: The scream gag copies a known Nox pattern too neatly, and 'Topsider! Bah! ...your lot cheat us miners' tries to build the world through a slur. That reads as a writer working from a template.

items.label: E
items.critique: These lines read as quest hooks with explicit instructions ('Smoke out their caves and bring back what they stole') and a planted lead with dashes and treasure detail. Nox's townsfolk are vaguer, and 'friend, the wolves will run from our torches' sounds stock.

items.label: F
items.critique: The hair joke and the 'not the miller' brush-off imitate Nox's non-sequitur humour, but they feel built to order. The middle line is a tidy post-quest acknowledgement with 'old [Person]'.

items.label: G
items.critique: These are short and plain enough to pass, but the opening names the player's class, which the packet says Westwood's text never does. 'I'm very busy' is a generic filler bark.

items.label: H
items.critique: Flat, slightly naive advice and a rumour that points to an in-game item (fire-walking boots). Unpolished and unforced, typical of Westwood's filler townsfolk.

items.label: I
items.critique: A random comic scream, then 'Have the Ogres been beaten, yet?' with its stray comma, then a half-finished rumour question. These are authentic quirks of the shipped text.

items.label: J
items.critique: There is repetition ('If you're smart you'll leave [Place], too') and cynical defeatism ('Let them take it, I say'). Plain, slightly clumsy, and tied to the main plot, as in the campaign.

tells: New texts turn townsfolk into quest dispensers: explicit instructions, locations and loot details ('hiding up on X', 'a whole chest of gold under his bed'), where Westwood's barks are vague rumours or moods.
New texts give a speaker a self-introduction with a lore purpose ('My name is X. I hunt... to keep the road safe'). Westwood's idle townsfolk seldom introduce themselves.
Comic barks in new texts reuse a Westwood formula (the scream plus a body-part or object gag, the deadpan brush-off) a little too exactly, and several stack up in one place.
Westwood's lines keep small mechanical flaws: missing full stops, stray commas, number mismatches, repetition. New texts are cleaner and use em-dash asides.
World-building slang or epithets ('Topsider', 'your lot') and stock fantasy cheer ('the wolves will run from our torches') read as another writer's voice.
Naming the player's class in a townsperson's line contradicts the class-free masking of Westwood's text.
